classes.official: An Amazon Associates program document, a Google Search Central document, or an FTC document. These are the only pages this project treats as able to settle a program or ranking rule.
classes.observed: The supplied affiliate short links and the Amazon listing pages they resolve to. Evidence about the artefact under test. Never used to state a program rule, and never used to state a product attribute the listing page does not print.
classes.carried: Read by an earlier session and published in that session's register. Not re-fetched by this session; quoted only where this session saw the text on the page.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements §6(t): customer reviews and star ratings
sources.quote: You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements for Creators API and PA API described in the License.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements §6(y): price tracking and price alerting
sources.quote: Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements §6(g): no incentive to use a Special Link
sources.quote: You will not offer any person or entity any consideration, reward, or incentive (including any money, rebate, discount, points, donation to charity or other organization, or other benefit) for using Special Links.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements §6(v) and §6(w): cloaking and link shortening
sources.quote: You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site.

sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement — §5 Identifying Yourself as an Associate
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”

sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement — §4: no representation about traffic or income
sources.quote: We do not make any representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the amount of traffic or commission income you can expect at any time in connection with the Associates Program, and we will not be liable for any actions you undertake based on your expectations.

sources.title: Associates Program — Application Review Process: the three-sales threshold and the tagged-link rule
sources.quote: After you sign up, our Associates team will check your application once you’ve driven qualified sales (we require at least three within the first 180 days).

sources.title: Associates Program — Application Review Process: the content bar for the declared Site
sources.quote: All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) – a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts. They must be publicly available (for example, they should not be a closed group, or behind a paywall).

sources.title: Associates Program — Application Review Process: recency and ownership
sources.quote: Content on your website must be recent (generally within the last 60 days). You must own your website.

sources.title: Associates Program — Application Review Process: what a Special Link tag is
sources.quote: Associates special links are the identifiers (e.g. abcd-20) embedded in Amazon product links. These tags must be embedded in your Amazon product links on the site(s) declared in your application.

sources.title: Google Search Central — spam policies: scaled content abuse
sources.quote: Scaled content abuse is when many pages are generated for the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings and not helping users. This abusive practice is typically focused on creating large amounts of unoriginal content that provides little to no value to users, no matter how it's created.

sources.title: Google Search Central — spam policies: thin affiliation, and what a good affiliate site is
sources.quote: Not every site that participates in an affiliate program is a thin affiliate. Good affiliate sites add value by offering meaningful content or features. Examples of good affiliate pages include offering additional information about price, original product reviews, rigorous testing and ratings, navigation of products or categories, and product comparisons.

sources.title: Google Search Central — guidance on generative AI content
sources.quote: However, using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users may violate Google's spam policy on scaled content abuse.

sources.title: Google Search Central — creating helpful, reliable, people-first content: the trending-topic warning
sources.page_dated_note: The page prints a last-updated line; this session's read captured the guidance sections but not the datestamp, so no date is asserted here.
sources.quote: Are you writing about things simply because they seem trending and not because you'd write about them otherwise for your existing audience?

sources.title: Google Search Central — creating helpful, reliable, people-first content: the spread-across-sites warning
sources.quote: Is the content mass-produced by or outsourced to a large number of creators, or spread across a large network of sites, so that individual pages or sites don't get as much attention or care?

sources.title: Google Search Central — creating helpful, reliable, people-first content: first-hand expertise
sources.quote: Does your content clearly demonstrate first-hand expertise and a depth of knowledge (for example, expertise that comes from having actually used a product or service, or visiting a place)?

sources.title: FTC — Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers: placement
sources.quote: The disclosure should be placed with the endorsement message itself.

sources.title: FTC — Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers: claims that require proof
sources.quote: You can’t talk about your experience with a product you haven’t tried.
